abstract: Background: Long non protein coding (lnc)RNAs are ubiquitous transcripts known to be major regulators of cellular processes in eukaryotes. In diatoms, specific lncRNA expression is tightly correlated to nutrient fluctuations, which suggests function, but their biological relevance remains to be established. In order to fill this knowledge gap, we sought to design a protocol to generate diatom lncRNA knockout mutants by CRISPR-Cas9 enabling subsequent functional studies to shed light into their mechanistic roles. Since lncRNAs do not contain open reading frames that can be targeted by point mutations for the generation of functional knockouts, we designed a multiplexed CRISPR-Cas9 plasmid harboring two independent gRNA for the specific ablation of lncRNA loci in P. tricornutum. As proof of concept, we used our plasmid-based system to target three phosphate depletion responsive lncRNAs. Results: Using the golden gate based uLoop system, we assembled a single plasmid containing all the necessary components to generate CRISPR-Cas9 large genomic ablations of lncRNAs in P. tricornutum using bacterial conjugation. Three intergenic lncRNAs (Linc91, Linc77 and Linc24) responsive to phosphate fluctuations were selected and independently targeted. Around 32% of the exconjugants presented a monoallelic ablation of the targeted loci and 11% presented a biallelic ablation on the first PCR-screening round. Mutated lines, harboring biallelic lncRNAs ablations for each lncRNA targeted, were successfully generated for each of the targeted lncRNAs. Additionally, a first line of phenotypic analysis revealed significant growth rate differences for one of the mutants ({Delta}Lnc24) under both full and phosphate depleted conditions, suggesting its involvement in cell division regulation under nutrient fluctuations. Conclusions: This work provides a simple and efficient method for the generation of lncRNA knock-out mutants in P. tricornutum. Furthermore, this approach can be easily adapted to other microalgae amenable to transformation, enabling the enhancement of our understanding of these important cellular regulatory transcripts in the marine environment.
